blocks.title: Chromatography
blocks.text: Chromatography is a method used primarily to separate the components of a mixture. It involves the distribution of a solute (the mixture) between a stationary phase and a mobile phase. The stationary phase may be a solid, or a liquid supported as a thin film on the surface of an inert solid; the mobile phase flowing over it may be a gas or a liquid.

Chromatography with a solid stationary phase is adsorption chromatography: a substance leaves the mobile phase to become adsorbed on the surface of the solid, as in thin layer chromatography (TLC) and column chromatography. Chromatography with a liquid stationary phase is partition chromatography: the substances being separated are distributed throughout both the stationary and the mobile phases, as in paper chromatography and gas-liquid chromatography.

blocks.caption: Two classes of chromatography

blocks.prompt: Differentiate adsorption from partition chromatography, and say why ink on a disputed document would be examined by chromatography (exercise Q.2k; MCQ IV).
blocks.explanation: In adsorption chromatography the stationary phase is a solid and the components separate by how strongly they stick to its surface; in partition chromatography the stationary phase is a liquid and they separate by how they distribute between the two liquids. Inks are mixtures of dyes, and each ink gives its own pattern of spots and Rf values, so chromatography of tiny samples shows whether two parts of a document were written with the same ink.

items: Chromatography: solute distributed between a stationary phase (solid, or liquid film on a solid) and a mobile phase (gas or liquid). Adsorption (solid stationary: TLC, column) and partition (liquid stationary: paper, gas-liquid).
